title: Identity Crisis
description: count_matches(a, b) counts the positions where two lists hold equal values. It works for small numbers.
hint: `is` asks "are these the same object?", not "are these equal?".
explanation: `is` compares identity: whether two names point to the same object in memory. CPython caches small integers (-5 to 256), so `is` happens to work for them, which hides the bug. Bigger numbers and most strings are separate objects. Use `==` to compare values. Keep `is` for `None`, `True` and `False`.
